name: Da Rang river
summary: The city sits at the mouth of the Đà Rằng, which the bureau also calls sông Ba. Cầu Đà Rằng has 21 spans and is called the longest bridge in central Vietnam on that page. No metre length is printed. Do not invent one. The bank is not given a ticket. Check on arrival.
timeNeeded: A look from the bank or the bridge. A clock was not printed.
getThere: The center, if you sleep in town.
heroCaption: The long bridge across the river, toward the sea

notice.title: No metre length is printed
notice.body: The bureau calls cầu Đà Rằng the longest bridge in central Vietnam and prints 21 spans. It does not print a length in metres. Do not invent one. The bank is not given a ticket.

body: The city sits where the Đà Rằng meets the sea. The bureau also calls the river sông Ba. Tháp Nhạn looks down on it from Núi Nhạn. The photograph from the hill shows the water, the town, and a bridge toward the sea. A night market on the bank was not on these pages. The center evening on the night page is Quảng trường 1/4.

Cầu Đà Rằng has 21 spans. The bureau calls it the longest bridge in central Vietnam and does not print a metre length. The long span in the photograph is that bridge. Count the spans on the page, not a length the page does not give.
The bank is not given a ticket. No visit clock was printed. Check on arrival. Minutes from Độc Lập were not printed.

figures.caption: The river from the hill, the town, and a nearer bridge toward the sea.
figures.alt: The Da Rang river from the hill in Tuy Hoa, with the town and a bridge toward the sea

gettingThere: The river is the center if you sleep in town. The tower hill is on the north bank, about 1,5 km from cửa Đà Diễn on the heritage page. Minutes from Độc Lập, and a taxi fare, were not printed. Check on arrival.

legs.body: The bridge and the bank are in town. No walking time was printed. Check on arrival.

legs.heading: From the tower hill
legs.body: The heritage page puts Tháp Nhạn on the north bank, about 1,5 km from cửa Đà Diễn. The view down is the river. The minutes were not printed.
